card.name: Davluri
card.tagline: Stately urban dance of Tbilisi's aristocracy
card.profile: Davluri is a city dance portraying the urban aristocracy of old Tbilisi (Wikipedia). Similar to the lyrical Kartuli but with simpler movements and a less formal male-female relationship, it is performed by many couples and, with its music and elaborate costumes resembling Georgian noble attire, simulates an aristocratic feast or ball on stage. The Georgian National Ballet's staged version was choreographed by Iliko Sukhishvili in 1948, with a new edition by Nino Ramishvili in 1980 (Sukhishvili/LCSD).
card.insight: Davluri occupies the courtly, urban end of the Georgian repertoire - a counterpart to the merchant Kintauri and craftsman Karachokheli city dances - illustrating how choreography maps social class in old Tiflis; Sukhishvili's female Davluri costumes can weigh up to ten kilos (hobbyblendfun).
card.image_significance: Georgia's aristocratic feast in motion. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — old Tbilisi, Georgia.
